summary: Jaisalmer Airport (JSA/VIJR) is a domestic airport located approximately 5 km south of Jaisalmer city in Rajasthan, India, serving the gateway to the Thar Desert. Operated jointly as a civil enclave within an Indian Air Force base, it primarily handles tourist traffic heading to the famous Golden City, known for its sandstone fort and camel safaris. The airport accommodates limited scheduled flights connecting to major Indian hubs like Delhi, Mumbai, and Jaipur.
faqs:
Q: How far is Jaisalmer Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is roughly 5 km (3 miles) south of Jaisalmer's main city, with a typical taxi ride taking about 15 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Jaisalmer Airport?
A: SpiceJet and previously Air India have operated scheduled services, with flights typically connecting to Delhi and seasonal routes during the Desert Festival period.

Q: Does Jaisalmer Airport operate 24 hours?
A: No, the airport operates during daylight hours only, with flight schedules aligned to daytime operations as it is a shared military airfield.

Q: Can I book a desert safari directly at the airport?
A: Yes, several tour operators and taxi drivers are available at the terminal offering camel safari packages and excursions to the Sam Sand Dunes.
transport_tips: Pre-paid taxi counters are available just outside the terminal, offering fixed-rate transfers to the city center and to Sam Sand Dunes for around 1,200-1,800 INR. Auto-rickshaws can also be hired for shorter trips into town, though they may not always be available at arrival times. Booking a hotel transfer in advance is recommended during the peak tourist season (October to March).
local_tip: Schedule an early morning flight if possible—temperatures in summer can soar above 45°C, and an afternoon arrival leaves you little time to explore the fort before sunset closes it. Many hotels also offer pickup services, so request one when booking to avoid haggling after a long journey.
